egress.terms: 'Unlimited Traffic, fair usage' on every storage plan. The Fair Use Policy states: 'DeluxHost does not apply hard caps or automatic blocks to the monthly traffic of its Services' and calculates combined inbound and outbound traffic during the calendar month. Indicative thresholds on German documentation cite 20 TB to 30 TB per month per storage service.

record.tooling: rclone SFTP, any backup tool, root KVM
record.chaining: Root KVM so MinIO or AList installs and can sit behind Cloudflare. RAID-5 is a single-parity array, weaker than AlphaVPS RAID-60 or ServaRica RAIDZ2.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: none. RAID-5 single parity. One drive failure tolerated per array, and the provider itself says in its LET threads 'Designed for backups, archives' and not 'a replacement for dedicated or enterprise servers'. Promo discount is 10% for 6 months on STORAGE-3 upward; STORAGE-1/-2 are already at list.
record.reliability_note: Small NL provider. Its own LET offer threads say 'Extremely limited stock' and it has run repeated waves of renewal price adjustments on its promo VPS lines ('DeluxHost = same quality with a deluxe price increase on first renewal', LET thread 213784). The storage line is explicitly excluded from that practice. 'Monthly pricing does not increase on renewal'. But the operator's history of repricing promo tiers is the single biggest caveat here.

record.interface_detail: a KVM-style VPS sold from a per-product cart; the cart's own network strings offer 'IPv6 only · 1× /64' or '{count}× IPv4 + 1× /64 IPv6', so the IPv6-only variant carries a routed /64 when it is selected.
record.tooling: any SSH client over IPv6; the cart is a client-rendered Next.js page, so a buyer should order in a browser
record.chaining: EUR 0.45 a month for 512 MB with a /64 is the cheapest annual row found, but the IPv6-only variant is not shown as a distinct plan on the vendor's page and the order path could not be read

limits.value: 'Unlimited Traffic, fair usage' with no published threshold - a discretionary throttle, not a quota

record.binding_note: fair use with no number is worse than a quota: there is no ceiling to design against and no threshold at which the node is safe.

identity_cost.detail: an account on the vendor's dashboard, which offers Google, GitHub and Discord sign-in plus email and password, and a passkey. The checkout form past the sign-in was not read. No card hold is stated.

record.confidence_note: the price, shape, stock flag and billing period are read from the vendor's own page, but the IPv6-only variant of X-0 is asserted only by a third-party forum post; the vendor's page does not label X-0 as IPv6-only and its FAQ says 'All our locations support native dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 connectivity'. The cart strings show an IPv6-only option exists, not that X-0 defaults to it.

evidence.proved: quoted plan card in the page's own data: 'X-0 ... 1 vCore ... 512MB DDR4 ... 10GB SSD ... 1Gbit/s Unlimited Traffic, fair usage ... price 6.00€ ... discountedPrice 5.40€ ... stock true ... orderUrl /cart?add=x-0&cycle=annually'

the cart page's own strings include '"ipv6Only":"IPv6 only · 1× /64"' and '"ipv4AndIpv6":"{count, plural, =1 {1× IPv4} other {#× IPv4}} + 1× /64 IPv6"' and an '"extraIpv4"' add-on priced '{price}/month per IP' - so an IPv6-only choice with a /64 exists in the cart, but the page body is client-rendered and the rendered cart was not read

third-party offer post, quoted: 'Offer X - X-0: €4/year, renewal €6/year ... 512 MB ... 10GB SSD ... Unlimited traffic (fair usage) ... IP Address: 0x IPv4 / 1 IPv6/64 ... Location: Amsterdam' - the source for treating X-0 as IPv6-only, and it prices the same product at EUR 4 with a EUR 6 renewal against the vendor's EUR 5.40

quoted FAQ in the page source: 'Yes. All our locations support native dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 connectivity. IPv6 is available on all plans at no additional cost.' - which contradicts a reading of X-0 as IPv6-only
the terms state that DeluxHost is a business owned by a sole trader, and carry an Italian VAT number

record.notes: The cheapest annual row found, and the one whose evidence is weakest exactly where it matters. The vendor page proves the price (EUR 5.40 discounted, EUR 6.00 list, in stock, annual), and the cart's own strings prove an IPv6-only-with-/64 option exists in the product. What no first-party page says is that X-0 is the IPv6-only variant: the vendor's FAQ claims all plans are dual-stack and IPv6 is free, while the forum post that put this row on the list says 0x IPv4. Both can be true if the cart defaults to IPv6-only and IPv4 is an add-on, but that is an inference and is recorded as one. A buyer should open the cart and read the network selector before paying. Not established: the rendered cart, the price of the extra-IPv4 add-on, payment rails, card hold, and the renewal price on the vendor's own page (the forum says EUR 6, which is the list price).

record.chaining: EUR 3.99 for 2 vCores, 4 GB and 50 GB of NVMe in the Netherlands with no metered transfer is the best ratio of RAM to price among evaluated providers after Advin, and 'unlimited, fair usage' suits a crawler front end that cannot predict its monthly bytes; the unmeasured fair-use clause is the risk, since the throttle point is unpublished.
